content: We are more often frightened than hurt; and we suffer more from imagination than from reality.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

Across his life and work, Seneca saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
